extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in algebraic geometry (readers of Vakil's 'The Rising Sea')
extracted.subtask_description: Statements, proofs, and exercises about Serre duality (for Hom and Ext), the identification of the dualizing sheaf, and the adjunction formula for subvarieties (especially Cartier divisors and regular embeddings) in the projective/Cohen–Macaulay setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functorial and trace Serre duality for Hom (Corollary 30.3.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: The functorial and trace versions of Serre duality for Hom hold for all equidimensional projective k-schemes (with no Cohen–Macaulay hypotheses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows by combining Proposition 30.3.11 with earlier results; the trace map for X appears as the diagonal arrow in diagram (30.3.11.1). No flatness hypotheses on π are needed here (unlike some vector-bundle/Ext propositions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Functorial Serre duality for Ext for finite flat cover of P^n (Proposition 30.3.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a Cohen–Macaulay projective k-scheme of pure dimension n and π: X → P^n is a finite flat morphism (as in Proposition 30.3.6(b)), then functorial Serre duality for Ext holds for X with dualizing sheaf ω_X := π^!_sh(ω_{P^n}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof parallels the δ-functor argument in §30.1.10: show Ext^i_X(F, π^!_sh(ω_{P^n})) ≅ H^{n-i}(X,F)∨ by checking both sides are universal δ-functors, using surjections from sums of O(−m), Serre vanishing, the projection formula, and functorial Serre duality for vector bundles on P^n.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functorial Serre duality for Ext for equidimensional Cohen–Macaulay projective schemes (Corollary 30.3.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Functorial Serre duality for Ext holds for all equidimensional Cohen–Macaulay projective k-schemes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine Proposition 30.3.13 with Proposition 30.3.6(b) and the projective-space case of earlier results (30.1.10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trace version of Serre duality for vector bundles (Remark 30.3.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: For vector bundles on equidimensional Cohen–Macaulay projective k-schemes, the Yoneda cup product followed by the trace map gives a functorial pairing Ext^i_X(F, ω_X) × H^{n-i}(X,F) → H^n(X,ω_X) → k, inducing the Serre duality isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One shows this particular pairing-induced map is a map of δ-functors; then by the universal δ-functor argument it is an isomorphism. The remark outlines extending earlier proofs to obtain the trace version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ext as O_X-module for closed embeddings (Preliminary Observation 30.4.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y is a closed embedding then for any O_Y-module F, Ext^i_Y(π_* O_X, F) naturally has the structure of an O_X-module; write it as π^{-1} Ext^i_Y(π_* O_X, F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute via an injective resolution of F by O_Y-modules and use adjointness and the fact that Hom_Y(π_* (–), –) carries an O_X-module structure; exercises point to coherence when Y and X are locally Noetherian.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of ω_X via Ext on ambient variety (Theorem 30.4.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a closed embedding π: X → Y of equidimensional projective k-schemes (dim X = n, dim Y = N) with Y satisfying functorial Serre duality for Ext and r = N − n, one has ω_X = π^{-1} Ext^r_Y(π_* O_X, ω_Y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof reduces to showing Hom_X(F, π^{-1}Ext^r_Y(π_* O_X, ω_Y)) ≅ H^n(X,F)∨ functorially in F, accomplished via Lemma 30.4.5 and functorial Serre duality on Y.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ext vanishing below codimension (Proposition 30.4.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the hypotheses of a closed embedding π: X → Y of equidimensional projective k-schemes with r = N − n, we have Ext^i_Y(π_* O_X, ω_Y) = 0 for all i < r.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses coherence of Ext sheaves, Serre vanishing (Theorem A), the local-to-global spectral sequence for Ext, and dimensional cohomology vanishing (cohomology vanishes above the dimension of support).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hom–Ext isomorphism for subvarieties (Lemma 30.4.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: For π: X → Y a closed embedding of codimension r with Y satisfying functorial Serre duality for Ext, there is a functorial isomorphism Hom_X(F, π^{-1}Ext^r_Y(π_* O_X, ω_Y)) ≅ Ext^r_Y(π_* F, ω_Y) for F in Coh_X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove by choosing an injective resolution of ω_Y, applying Hom_Y(π_* F, –), using adjointness to view as Hom_X(F, π^!_sh I^i), and analyzing the resulting complex; several exercises guide the splitting and exactness before the r-th step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjunction formula for effective Cartier divisors (formula and Proposition 30.4.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Y is a Cohen–Macaulay projective scheme of pure dimension N satisfying functorial Serre duality for Ext and X ⊂ Y is an effective Cartier divisor (hence Cohen–Macaulay), then ω_X = ω_Y(X)|_X. In particular, if ω_Y is invertible then so is ω_X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute π^{-1}Ext^1_Y(π_* O_X, ω_Y) using the short exact sequence 0 → O_Y(−X) → O_Y → O_X → 0, apply Hom(–, ω_Y) and truncate; the identification ω_X = coker(ω_Y → ω_Y⊗ O_Y(X)) = ω_Y(X)|_X is canonical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dualizing sheaf for complete intersections in P^n (Exercise 30.4.F)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a complete intersection in P^n of hypersurfaces of degrees d_1,…,d_r, then ω_X ≅ det Ω_X; furthermore, if X is smooth then ω_X ≅ O_X(−n−1 + Σ d_i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use that complete intersections are Cohen–Macaulay and apply the adjunction formula for K (see Exercise 21.5.B); Serre duality hypotheses are satisfied via Corollary 30.3.14.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ext and determinant-of-normal-sheaf identification for regular embeddings (Exercise 30.4.G)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Y is smooth equidimensional and π: X → Y is a codimension-r regular embedding with normal sheaf N_{X/Y} locally free, and L an invertible sheaf on Y, then (a) Ext^i_Y(π_* O_X, L) = 0 for i ≠ r, and (b) there is a canonical isomorphism π^{-1} Ext^r_Y(π_* O_X, L) ≅ (det N_{X/Y})^∨ ⊗_O_X (L|_X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a local question (no projectivity needed); for regular embeddings compute Ext via a locally free resolution and relate the top Ext to determinant of the normal bundle tensored with the restriction of L.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dualizing sheaf for regular embeddings in projective space; ω_X invertible and equals K_X when smooth (IMPORTANT Exercise 30.4.H)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a codimension-r regular embedding in P^n_k (hence Cohen–Macaulay), then ω_X = π^{-1} Ext^r_{P^n}(π_* O_X, ω_{P^n}) ≅ (det N_{X/P^n})^∨ ⊗ ω_{P^n}|_X; in particular ω_X is invertible. If X is a smooth pure codimension-r subvariety then ω_X ≅ K_X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Exercise 30.4.G with L = ω_{P^n} and use that regular embeddings in projective space are Cohen–Macaulay; use adjunction for Ω to identify with canonical bundle in the smooth case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application: canonical bundle is Serre-dualizing (Remark 30.4.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: The version of Serre duality given in Theorem 18.5.1 follows by combining Corollary 30.3.10 with Exercise 30.4.I, i.e., the canonical bundle K_X is Serre-dualizing under the stated hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ties the adjunction and Ext-identifications back to the earlier Serre duality statements; exercises earlier in the section show how the identification of ω_X with K_X (when applicable) yields the classical Serre duality result.
